auth_check.reason: No login/credential endpoint exists in endpoint_catalog.json or the recording; no cookies, bearer tokens, or CSRF tokens appeared. All state-changing endpoints (/api/order/cancel, /api/order/refund/*, /api/order/price-adjustment) are reachable without any principal. Per the contract, a flow with no login/credential endpoint records auth_check.performed=false. The absence of authentication is recorded separately as F-009 (agent hypothesis, unverified, NOT_EXECUTED); scope.json does not set authentication_required:true, so this is treated as unconfirmed coverage, not a confirmed bypass.

invariant_note: All monetary scenarios assert the approved Northstar bound: order.totalReturned must not exceed order.originalAmount (sum_lte, 100 > 100 = false). Each script establishes a fresh state via POST /api/demo/reset, captures its own before/actions/after from the harness-assigned flowbusters_sequence, and computes violation.observed from its own AFTER read.

findings.title: State-changing payout endpoints require no authentication (broken access control, unverified)

execution.missing_precondition: The fixture has no login endpoint, no second principal, and no per-user order ownership (single order #1042, all actions unauthenticated). A broken-access-control / IDOR finding cannot be demonstrated without two distinct principals acting on a shared resource.
execution.next_step: Provide an authed build with a second user who does not own order #1042; attempt GET /api/order and a state change (cancel/refund) using that second user's session, and verify ownership is enforced server-side. Note scope.json does not set authentication_required:true, so this remains an unconfirmed coverage gap, not a confirmed finding.

evidence.summary: Every state-changing endpoint in the catalog (cancel, refund/request, refund/complete, price-adjustment) and the recording responded 200 with no credentials present. This is consistent with a missing auth boundary but is NOT proof of a defect: the demo app may be intentionally auth-free. Retained as a review item so the missing boundary is not silently treated as safe.

findings.title: Cancel + refund-complete interleaving can stack two reimbursements on order #1042

evidence.summary: Cancels a fresh order then drives refund/complete (and the reverse order, and a concurrent race). If both the cancellation reimbursement and a completed refund pay out, order.totalReturned could exceed order.originalAmount.

findings.title: Refund/complete is callable with no auth and no prior refund request

evidence.summary: Calls refund/complete directly on a fresh order, bypassing refund/request and any authentication. A completed payout with no prior request or no principal would be a workflow-authorization flaw.

findings.title: Cancel honors a client-supplied reimbursementAmount larger than the fixed $100
findings.expected: IGNORED/CLAMPED (server recomputes reimbursement from order state)

evidence.summary: Sends a JSON body with reimbursementAmount=1000 on the (otherwise bodyless) cancel. Violation true iff order.totalReturned exceeds order.originalAmount, i.e. the server trusted the client amount.

findings.title: Replaying the cancel request can issue a second $100 reimbursement
findings.expected: IDEMPOTENT (second cancel no-ops; totalReturned stays <= originalAmount)

evidence.summary: Cancels, then replays the identical cancel (and a concurrent double-cancel race). A second reimbursement would push totalReturned to 200 > 100.

findings.title: Price adjustment can stack on a completed refund to exceed original amount
findings.expected: HOLD (adjustment blocked once refund completed, or total capped at originalAmount)

evidence.summary: Combines the $30 price-protection adjustment with the full refund request->complete chain in both orders plus a concurrent adjustment+complete race, then re-reads totalReturned vs originalAmount.

findings.title: Refund request accepts a client-supplied requestedAmount far above the order total
findings.expected: CLAMPED to order total (requestedAmount must not exceed originalAmount)

evidence.summary: Sends requestedAmount=99999 to refund/request then completes it. Primary predicate checks totalReturned<=originalAmount; the request-clamp rule (requestedAmount<=originalAmount) is reported as an unsupported_business_rule review item because a payout cap could mask a large accepted requestedAmount.

findings.title: Price adjustment can still pay out on a canceled/reimbursed order
findings.expected: REJECTED after cancel (order terminal, already reimbursed)

evidence.summary: Runs cancel + price-adjustment in both orders and a concurrent race; if the $30 adjustment applies on top of the $100 cancellation reimbursement, totalReturned exceeds originalAmount (violates UIR-003 'price protection not available while another order request is active').

findings.title: Price adjustment still applies to an order already canceled and reimbursed (terminal-state bypass)
findings.expected: REJECTED (order terminal per observed UI rule UIR-001)

evidence.summary: Cancels the order, then bypasses the removed 'Request price adjustment' button and calls the endpoint directly. Violation true iff the adjustment still increments totalReturned past originalAmount.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to all order state-changing endpoints (coverage gap)

evidence.summary: The recording shows no login, session cookie, bearer token, or CSRF token, and all state-changing endpoints were invoked without any principal. scope.json does not set authentication_required:true, so per contract this is NOT confirmed as a missing-authentication vulnerability. It is an agent hypothesis worth verifying: if this is the intended deployment, any anonymous caller can cancel/adjust/refund any order id (the flow uses a fixed order #1042 with no per-user scoping), which would be CWE-862/CWE-306.

execution.missing_precondition: No second, differently-scoped principal exists in the fixture to demonstrate broken object-level access control; the app exposes a single fixed order #1042 with no user identity.
execution.next_step: Confirm with the product owner whether authentication/authorization is in scope for this endpoint set. If it is, prepare two user fixtures each owning an order and attempt to read/act on the other user's order using the first user's session.

results.error_message: Missing precondition: no second principal / order ownership in the fixture to demonstrate broken access control.

execution.missing_precondition: No login endpoint, no second principal, and no per-user order ownership (single order #1042).
execution.next_step: Provision a second user who does not own order #1042 and attempt read + state change under that session to test server-side ownership enforcement.

summary.note: Draft review-only statuses. The backend executes each script once, captures signed HTTPX transport evidence, and recomputes the sum_lte(invariant) verdict from the captured AFTER response. A violation.observed=false (control held) promotes the result to NOT_REPRODUCED; a true (control failed) promotes to CONFIRMED with the finding retained. F-009 is a NOT_EXECUTED coverage gap.
